id: title:charlesvien:react on the triggering message not the thread root

review.posthog_relevance: Adds a guard clause and corresponding test to the Slack app's message threading logic, preventing unnecessary Slack API calls when the thread context lacks a specific user message timestamp.
review.reason: Score 1 assigned. The change is a narrow, localized maintenance improvement: it adds a guard clause to skip Slack API calls when a timestamp is missing and includes a parameterized test to verify this behavior. This does not demonstrate a broader systemic capability or critical reliability improvement, nor does it establish unverified outcomes like incident avoidance. The relevance
review.uncertainty: The actual benefit depends on the frequency of this edge case in production, which is not established by the code alone. No other tier-3 systemic safeguards or tier-2 substantive capability improvements are present.

observations.behavior: Adds a guard clause: if user_message_ts is None, the method returns early without removing the existing reaction or adding a new one.
observations.posthog_connection: This could prevent Slack API calls when the thread context lacks a specific user message timestamp, potentially avoiding unnecessary API invocations or handling edge cases where the mention is not the root of the thread.

observations.behavior: Adds a parameterized test with varying user_message_ts values and updates assertions to check that no API calls are made when user_message_ts is None.
observations.posthog_connection: This could help verify that the Slack integration correctly skips API calls when the expected message timestamp is missing, rather than failing or making unintended requests.
